section.data-name: The Virtual Roadshow You Shouldn't Miss

h1.font: Partnership Knowledge Base, Documentation & Forum: all the extra resources you need

section.class: s_text_block pt40 pb40 o_colored_level undefined o_cc o_cc1

div.p: If you have come this far, you must have seen that we have got lots of documentation in this course. However, while this course is specifically about your growth as a Project Lead, we are maybe a bit "light" on some aspects, like the commercial ones and how we communicate together. If you want to discover more of these aspects and dig deeper in how we collaborate, this task is for you.
We suggest that you have, at the very least, a quick look at these sources of information. We guarantee that there isn’t a single project where you don’t need at least one of these life savers.

When you start your kick-off meeting, and during the whole implementation, the customer will give you a lot of information about their business, their requirements, and their constraints. Understanding what the customer is doing requires some deep business knowledge that you probably do not have yet, and to a certain extent, you will never have as it is impossible to know everything about every business. To avoid getting lost during the process and to help you structure the discussions, the expert team* has created some tools to help you better analyze and understand the customer's business. Those tools are called the "Mind Map" and currently cover six topics:

ul.li: Logistic
Accounting
Manufacturing
Website / ecommerce
Marketing
Point of Sales

div.p: By using this tool:

ul.li: You will be able to approach the Kick-off Phase with confidence as the Mind Maps will help to structure the analysis and not forgetting important questions to ask to your customer.
You will be able to better phase the implementation.
You will receive guidance to properly implement an application without forgetting important configurations or recommendations.
You will increase your Product Knowledge application by application.

div.p: In other terms, you will implement the project efficiently, deliver it quickly, and avoid mistakes that could lead to frustration for the customer, and potential project failure. But most importantly it will give you more confidence in the first steps of any implementation.

ul.li: Cover most configuration decisions you have to make with your customer and explain the business logic behind them.
Give you the best practices for each application.
Warn you about possible traps to avoid making long-lasting mistakes.
Act as a minimum viable configuration checklist.

div.p: Since those aspects are really broad, the Mind Maps cannot be exhaustive. You will have to use critical thinking and your own experience to cover all the points to be discussed during the kick-off meeting, and what should be implemented. Hence the Mind Maps can never be a substitute for the Business Analysis, but should be used either as a first step in this process or as an additional tool to improve this skill.

p.span: How to read and naviguate mindmaps?

div.p: Mindmaps are split into four main sections:

ul.li: Generic Principles: the main commandments to keep in mind at all the time. For instance, the localization setting when you implement Accounting.
Master Data: the configuration points and their associated recommendations.
Basic Flows: the flows to review for sure with your customer (and train them accordingly). For instance, the pricelist in the e-commerce flow.
Advanced Flows: the most advanced flows, usually to be kept for a later stage. For instance, the Asset management in Accounting.

div.p: Then, within each section > sub-topic > particular node, you can refer to the following legend to navigate through the information provided:

ul.li: Section
Subtopic
Particular node

li.font: must do or mandatory IF thumbs up
business need or configuration reason (question mark)

strong.font: Here you will find our mind maps

div.p: Have a look at the Partnership knowledge base. This partner-dedicated course is all about giving you more weapons when it comes to collaborating with Odoo:

ul.li: How to get some help from my account manager?
Which are the advantages of Odoo Enterprise vs Odoo community?
Which extra services Odoo can propose in order to help me put my client in production?
How to use the partner dashboards?

div.p: These are some of the questions that are answered and will help you get started on the track of a successful partnership.

The root of all our functional documentation can be found at the following address, but do not forget that you will find the tech doc (including installation and API doc) next to it in case you need it. While the doc does not cover ALL the functional nor technical aspects, it has been growing in size and popularity over the years and is more reliable than ever.

If you wish to contribute, you can do it in several ways. You can first offer your own pull request on the GitHub repository, if you know how to do it. If you do not, do not hesitate to propose some improvement on that doc when discussing this course item with your Odoo Onboarder. If we receive a lot of similar demands, there are high chances that the missing documentation will be added soon.

is an unstructured StackOverflow-like place where you will find an answer to very specific questions. If you find a blocking point, chances are high that someone already fixed it and posted a comment on somebody else's question in the Forum. Navigate through it with the different search options, and if you cannot find what you need, Google it. Google very often redirects to our Odoo forum if you have "odoo" next to your tech or functional question.

In addition to every public comment on the Forum, you will find a lot of comments of our consultants. You will find superstars like Ray Carnes, our functional living legend at Odoo, but also lots of questions asked by our own employees and answered by some other, more senior, Odoo employees. While it might seem strange, we decided a few months ago to make all of our internal questions public. So when an Odoo employee has a question for one of their colleagues, they are required to put it on the forum and ask for help so that it does not only gets solved for them, but for all the Odoo community.
Do not hesitate to follow the "Quickstart" tag to follow all the question posted by an Odoo employee. These are Odoo verified answers, so you can trust them.
On this channel, you'll find all the videos that we record internally at Odoo. Topics range from ‘what's new’ in a specific app, to the explanation of a complex flows.
If you are a more visual learner and you have a question, don't hesitate to check the channel to see if your answer isn't in one of the thousands of videos we have.
If you like to be updated on the latest and general news about Odoo, follow us on X (formerly Twitter).

This task is about making you see other important references and documentation sources directly available to you. These three sources are a concentration of information and should be essential tools in your toolbox.

You are now made aware of these three very important sources of extra information at Odoo and are better prepared to face your client's needs. Do not hesitate to add your comments in both the Partnership Knowledge Base (PKB) and the forum, or to upvote answers, you found useful on the forum.

p.b: Implementing the POS (Point of Sales) application is never easy as it requires knowledge about hardware and infrastructure, regulations (black box)... This use case aims to give you a better understanding of the module but also on the way to deal with all the external requirements that are part of the proper implementation of this module.

div.p: Before the session:

ul.li: Create a database and make the use case.
If you have the hardware: Install an IOT BOX and print a ticket as evidence you connected a printer with the IOT box.

div.p: During the session (with the consultant):

ul.li: Ask your questions about the case.
Discuss your answers.

div.p: The complexity of the sales at the counter hides more than you could think of. This task will help you to have a first look at the complexity and constraints of the POS implementation before having your first project.

section.data-name: The Virtual Roadshow You Shouldn't Miss

div.p: The purpose of this use case is to simulate a kick-off call with the owner of a restaurant: Pépé Café. He just purchased 50 hours of consulting and is very excited about launching Odoo in his restaurant.
He purchased the following apps:

ul.li: Sales
PoS
Invoicing
Inventory

div.p: After having introduced yourself and the methodology, your SPOC starts to explain his business.

In addition to our catering service, we offer our customers the possibility to eat in our shop. Concretely, we have a display case with the daily meals we prepare. We have a fridge where we stock all our orders. We also have some tables where our customers can eat: 6 tables close to our display case and 3 tables on our terrace.
In summary, we offer 3 main services to our customers :

ul.li: Eat in our shop
Purchase and direct pickup
Purchase and later shipping

div.p: I will now give you more information about our need for each service.
Customers can eat our daily meals at our shop’s tables.

ul.li: As previously mentioned, we have 6 tables inside and 3 tables on the terrace. We have 4 product categories: drinks, appetizers, main courses, and desserts. We want our waiter to find the tables and meals as easily as possible. We would like to make it as visual as possible. Could we add pictures to make it clearer?
I want my waiter to use a tablet to book the orders. He also must be able to put a note in the kitchen to keep track of information for each meal.

We have wine and beer recommendations for every meal we sell. We want our waiter to easily have access to them to give the best service to our customers. We have a large wine and beer panel, and we do not want him to lose much time in searching manually for the beverages. Can we add this information for each meal? Do you have a tool to select the recommended beverages easily?

Sometimes, customers want to split the bills. You know, nobody wants to pay for the entire table... Sometimes they want to pay for what they ate, sometimes they just want to divide by the number of guests. I want a tool that allows us to easily split the bill in both ways.
I don’t want my waiter to lose time to find who ordered something. When a table wants to pay the bill, I want my waiter to be able to directly check the total.
My waiter often receives tips. How can he handle them?
In my shop, I also would like my customers to order by themselves but only for the category drinks & food. I would like my food category to be displayed at first place
I would like my customers to be able to book a table but only for inside floor (6 tables of 4-person capacity). How can I see the bookings?

I have 5 students working at the same time in the same computer, is it possible not to have 5 users for them? I would like them to connect through a code to recognize them and I have a very high turnover because they are students. I would like only the manager to be able to close the session, is it possible?

I have a menu. Can I realize it in Odoo? I would also like to let the choice for the sauces but they can select several sauces, how can I do that? How can I communicate with my kitchen ? Can I see if the order is ready or not? Can I choose which products are sent to the bar and which ones to the kitchen?

People would be allowed to order through a kiosk. I would like customers to be able to take out but in my country, the tax applied is different (in Belgium, tax is 21% when you eat in the restaurant and only 6% when you take out), how to apply it in a specific order?

div.p: They can buy meals from our display case and take them directly back home.

ul.li: How can I handle those orders with the POS? These customers are not eating at a table but I do not want to use another point of sale for these kinds of sales.
As you probably know, the tax they pay is lower if they order take-away. The final price is the same for me, but the tax is different. How could I handle this?

A lot of my customers are coming during their lunchtime as they are working in the neighborhood. It happens that a customer forgets to ask for the ticket to be reimbursed by their employer. I want to be able to print tickets until 1 week after the day of the order. For example, a customer came to the restaurant this Monday, and when they got back to the office, they realized that they forgot to ask for their ticket. They came back to the restaurant on the next Monday and asked me to print out their ticket from the previous time. How can I do this? Could I also reprint an invoice?

div.p: They can order meals in advance and be delivered later. This option is commonly used for birthdays or business events. We deliver food and beverages. We have a large panel of really good wine…

ul.li: For this service, clients are used to reaching us by phone or email. Those orders are generally quite long. We do not take them in the display case, we would create too much queue. They explain what they want and when they want to be delivered. If it’s a business party, it is on the date of the event.

To confirm the order, we ask them to pay a 30% down payment directly in our shop. The delivery boy will ask them to pay for the rest at the moment he ships the order. They must be able to ask for an invoice because we also work for companies directly.

Talking about payments: we have different payment methods. In the shop, we use cash and Adyen. When we do the deliveries, the client can pay by cash or by SumpUp Air (Portable Payment Terminal). Are our payment terminals integrated with Odoo? I saw on your website that you have some kind of hardware to connect all devices to the point of sale. Is it mandatory to use it with my payment terminal? What about other devices?
These kinds of customers are not always drinking everything we sell. We usually offer to refund each bottle that has not been opened. How could I handle this?

p.b: We sometimes have to take cash from our cash register during the day. For example: to buy some cleaning products. How can we easily do it? I do not want to lose time closing my POS session.

div.p: We always seek to improve our customers' loyalty. Indeed, we have decided to have a new loyalty program implemented within Odoo. We are looking for a scoring system based on the total amount spent by our customers and we would like to assess one point for each euro spent and to reward the customer with a discount of 20 euros on the next dinner when 150 points are reached. Moreover, I want a monthly report to evaluate the amount of total points scored by each customer. How can I achieve this?

Christmas is good for our business because, you know… But as you may know, the month after is always more complicated. That’s why, every year in January, we propose a 10% discount to our customers if they use a specific promotion code that we sent by email before. Is it possible to use such a feature?

We give the possibility to buy gift cards for family and friends. Those gift cards come from a supplier, so they come with a previously defined code and amounts. How can I enter those cards in the database?
With this task you should be able to:

ul.li: Know the basic features and constraints of the POS application.
Know how to install the IOT BOX.
Handle different business constraints for a shop/restaurant.

div.p: You should have a better overview of what it requires to think of when implementing the POS. You should also have a better idea of the configuration options of the POS.
